headline: Directed staff to begin a strategic investment budget for Fiscal Year 2028, 4-0; consent agenda also approved 4-0.
summary: The council heard a presentation from a Tax the Rich to Fund Vermont coalition member asking for council support for a town meeting ballot measure. It also reviewed goal updates and discussed ways to involve residents in the FY2028 budget. The council approved the consent agenda and directed staff to begin a strategic investment budget.
decisions: Approved the consent agenda, including prior minutes, payroll and accounts payable warrants, reports, and VLCT designations, 4-0.
Directed City Manager Wang and staff to begin budget work on a strategic investment budget for FY28, 4-0.
No motion was taken on council engagement on the city budget, as the council determined none was necessary.

decision_evidence.quote: Motion to approve the consent agenda by Councilor Turkos, seconded by Councilor Goodrich. Motion carried 4-0.
Motion by Councilor Turkos to direct City Manager Wang and Staff to begin the budget work on a strategic investment budget, seconded by Councilor Goodrich. Motion carried 4-0.
After discussion it was determined that no motion was necessary for this item.

Councilor Eli Ogilvie: I want to apologize. Last month's MIC meeting was unfortunately canceled due to

V. City Updates 
 
Elaine Wang, City Manager, gave the following updates: 
 
Are you a resident with an extra vehicle? Are you a college student, business owner, or employee 
looking for a steady parking option? Need a spot in the parking garage during winter parking bans? Just 
looking for a place to park? The City of Winooski is now offering long-term parking space agreements 
in the Winooski Parking Garage on Cascade Way to individuals or households. Multi-month and 
month-to-month agreements are available – to learn more and ﬁll out the inquiry survey to get started, 
please visit winooskivt.gov/news.  
 
The General Election is Tuesday, November 3rd, from 7 AM to 7 PM at the Winooski Senior Center. The 
Vermont Secretary of State will mail ballots to registered and active Winooski voters beginning in October, 
using the address on your voter registration. This is your ballot! Once you receive your ballot, you can return it 
by mail to Winooski City Hall, drop it off at the City Clerk’s Ofﬁce, or bring it to the Winooski Senior Center on 
Election Day. You can check your ballot status and register to vote at vote.vermont.gov. 
VI. Regular Items 
A. Discussion: Presentation from "Tax the Rich to Fund Vermont" Coalition Member - Mayor Thomas 
Renner 
 
Minutes: Winooski resident Matt Gile, a coalition member from "Tax the Rich Fund Vermont" discussed 
their initiative to get a measure on the town meeting day ballot that proposes raising taxes on the 
wealthiest 5% of Vermonters in order to help pay for various social programs that have had funding 
cuts. They would like to collect over 300 signatures and are carrying out this initiative in several 
Vermont communities. They would like the support of the Winooski City Council. Mayor Renner stated 
that before the start of the legislative session, municipalities send lists of their priorities to the 
legislature. If this ballot measure is passed by voters, and/or the City Council recommends items to the 
legislature, it does not mean the measure is enacted. We are demonstrating what we want, we are not 
implementing the measure until there is legislative action. Mr. Gile stated that if the measure passes it 
would be advising Council to inform the legislature that they should be imposing a tax on the top 5% of 
income earners in order to fund robust social programming. 
 
B. Discussion/Approval: Fiscal Year 2028 Budget Goal Setting - Angela Aldieri, Finance Director, and 
Elaine Wang, City Manager 
 
Minutes: City Manager Wang reviewed the memorandum from Finance Director Aldieri regarding the 
FY28 goal discussion. Strategic vs. level services vs. level funded budgets was discussed. A strategic 
budget would allow for updating costs for existing services and allocating additional resources to 
priority areas. A level services budget allows for costs to existing services to be updated for estimated 
increases due to inflation and cost of living increases but does not increase funding to catch up on 
deficiencies. Level funded would essentially mean a reduction in the budget due to inflation.

Discussion followed regarding the difficulty of budget discussions as there are so many things that 
Council would like to do while recognizing the reality that our residents are living in. It was brought up 
that residents do not want to pay higher taxes, but they also would like services as well as 
infrastructure repairs. There is a need to explain to residents where investments are going. Council 
members indicated that level services or level funded budgets are not feasible as it hurts the city in the 
long run, even if it is financially appealing. All indicated they prefer a strategic approach.  
 
Motion: Motion by Councilor Turkos to direct City Manager Wang and Staff to begin the budget work on 
a strategic investment budget, seconded by Councilor Goodrich. Motion carried 4-0. 
 
C. Discussion: Goal Update - Elaine Wang, City Manager 
 
Minutes: City Manager Wang provided highlights from the memos in the Council Packet regarding Goal 
Updates. For cross-cutting (tasks that affect more than one vision area of the comprehensive plan), 
items discussed were the Cascades parking garage and the status of the renting of spaces and revenue 
generation. City Manager Wang thanked Finance Director Aldieri for her work on single space rentals. 
Approaches to stabilizing the parking fund were discussed such as outreach to landlords and their 
tenants, as well as the status and logistics of mass mailings. Regarding economic vitality, the work of 
the Community Liaison for the Burlington Winooski bridge replacement project was discussed. The 
liaison is facilitating an advisory group task force focusing on business engagement both in Burlington 
and Winooski, as well as representatives from the Vermont Agency of Transportation. A business 
engagement support plan has been drafted. City Manager Wang stated it was heartening to see how 
supportive the state is and the regional partners are.  
 
Regarding Economic Vitality, initiatives of the Economic Mobility Manager Cymone Bedford were 
discussed. This includes a workshop related to a business networking and learning series, developing a 
community program to help people get engaged in governance, and regular economic communities of 
practice meetings for each focus area.  
 
There are highlights related to Housing, which Housing Initiatives Director Jazmine Hurley will present 
at a future meeting.  
 
City Manager Wang stated that Paul Sarne, Communications Director, has been doing a great job 
maintaining the language access procedure. He just finished the first update of the language list with 
the help of the Winooski School District. 
 
Questions and discussion from Council involved use of lawn signs with QR codes to invoke feedback 
from residents regarding he comprehensive plan, avoiding “survey fatigue”, a request for updates on 
the Senior Center now that there is full-time staff, and outreach to the public regarding parking garage 
space availability.  
 
D. Discussion/Approval: Council Engagement on City Budget - Councilor Al Turkos 
 
Minutes: Councilor Turkos discussed their thoughts regarding expanding community participation in the 
FY2028 budget process. The goal would to not just focus on attendance at meetings but also to create other 
opportunities for residents to learn about the budget and have input in the budgeting process. Items discussed 
included doing year-round outreach, that every conversation should be a budget outreach, and how priorities 
come from hearing from the people in the community. There are items people want that are not feasible, but 
something else may alleviate the situation.

As an example, the new bus route to Shaw's in lieu of having a grocery store in the City. Outreach to the 
school system in the form of the Youth Budget Lab was discussed, along with the possibility of reaching out to 
school staff to identify classes that might want to meet with City Councilors. Bringing the “budget game” to 
the farmer's market was discussed as well as "Council in the Community" and the need to identify events 
where the Council could go to the community rather than the community come to them. Engaging with people 
when quarterly taxes are due was discussed, with the idea that taxes are first and foremost on taxpayers’ 
mind at that time. Use of a shared document for Councilors to input conversations and questions was 
discussed. City Manager Wang asked to be kept informed of events that City Council will be attending.  
 
Motion: After discussion it was determined that no motion was necessary for this item. 
 
VII. Adjourn 
 
Motion: Motion by to adjourn at 7:24 PM by Councilor Turkos, seconded by Councilor Goodrich. Motion 
carried 4-0.
